audits.title: 543 Improving the Management of Acute Ureteric Colic in A Multi-Centre District General Hospital: A Closed-Loop Audit
audits.standard: BAUS 2018 guidance on acute ureteric colic, including clinic follow-up within 4 weeks
audits.setting: Multi-centre district general hospital, Sandwell and West Birmingham Hospitals NHS Trust (A&E and urology)
audits.intervention: Teaching sessions for doctors and nurses in A&E and urology.

cycle2.result: Serum calcium 60.4%, CT KUB within 24 hours 97.7%, NSAIDs 67.2% (increases of 20.4%, 0.4% and 5.2%); only 26.4% seen in clinic within 4 weeks, mean wait 41 days.

audits.other_findings: Only 31.3% had acute surgical intervention; a daily emergency theatre slot and computerised clinic booking are recommended.
audits.citation: Desai C, Bruce A, Ehsanullah S, Otite U, Ahmad S. 543 Improving the Management of Acute Ureteric Colic in A Multi-Centre District General Hospital: A Closed-Loop Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab259.065.

audits.title: WE6.8 An audit to look at the current practice of treating ureteric stones and compare it to NICE/ BAUS guidelines
audits.standard: NICE and BAUS guidelines on ureteric stones (CT within 24 hours)
audits.setting: Chesterfield Royal Hospital, emergency department renal colic presentations

cycle1.result: Average time to CT 16 hours 31 minutes; 6% (3) had definitive inpatient surgery; 62% conservative, 26% stent, 4% nephrostomy.

audits.other_findings: Patients with stents or nephrostomy waited about 7 weeks for definitive treatment.
audits.citation: Minhas A, Moss B. WE6.8 An audit to look at the current practice of treating ureteric stones and compare it to NICE/ BAUS guidelines. British Journal of Surgery. 2022;109(Supplement_5). doi:10.1093/bjs/znac248.151.

audits.title: 1033 Renal Colic Emergency Management - an Audit Cycle
audits.standard: BAUS and NICE renal colic recommendations: CT within 14 hours, NSAIDs, referral criteria
audits.setting: Emergency department, Aneurin Bevan University Health Board, Newport

cycle1.result: NSAIDs prescribed 87%; CT within 14 hours 93%; 100% meeting referral criteria referred; 67% not meeting referral criteria referred.

audits.intervention: Updated NSAID dosing and updated health board renal colic pathway.

cycle2.result: NSAIDs prescribed 50%; CT within 14 hours 100%; 50% not meeting referral criteria referred.

audits.other_findings: Low numbers; all patients having CT KUB suggested as a better identifier for future audits.
audits.citation: Mercer R, Jose M. 1033 Renal Colic Emergency Management - an Audit Cycle. British Journal of Surgery. 2023;110(Supplement_7). doi:10.1093/bjs/znad258.173.

audits.title: 380 Audit of the Management of Suspected Ureteric Colic in Barnet Hospital Emergency Department
audits.standard: BAUS/NICE guidelines for suspected ureteric colic
audits.setting: Barnet Hospital emergency department, Royal Free London NHS Trust

cycle1.result: 98% had CT-KUB within 14 hours (mean 4 hours 50 minutes); 52% received analgesia in ED (mean 3 hours 26 minutes from triage); calcium measured in 51% and urate in 4%.

audits.intervention: Education and pathway review; second cycle in progress
audits.other_findings: 22% had an obstructing stone; 75% of these were referred to the stone MDT and 45% had repeat CT-KUB requested.

audits.title: 1167 A Closed Loop Audit to Benchmark Care for Emergency Department Attendances with Renal Colic
audits.standard: NICE quality standards for assessment and management of renal colic (CTKUB timing, NSAID analgesia, time to urological intervention, bone profile/calcium, stone diet advice)
audits.setting: Emergency departments, St Helier and Epsom hospitals (Epsom & St Helier Hospitals, London)

cycle1.result: CTKUB reported within 24 hours 97.9%; NSAIDs 54.5%; surgical intervention within 48 hours 70%; calcium requested 77.9%; dietary/fluid advice 8.7%

audits.intervention: Patient leaflet on stone diet and a renal order-set, plus raising clinician awareness

cycle2.result: CTKUB reported within 24 hours 100%; NSAIDs 71.9%; surgical intervention within 48 hours 100%; calcium requested 94.7%; dietary/fluid advice 39.4%

audits.other_findings: Dietary and lifestyle advice improved but remained low at 39.4%.
audits.citation: Dehbokri A, Mayer C, Ariyanayagam D. 1167 A Closed Loop Audit to Benchmark Care for Emergency Department Attendances with Renal Colic. British Journal of Surgery. 2024;111(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znae163.302.

audits.title: 195 Close Loop Retrospective Audit of Acute Ureteric Stone Management: A Comparison with NICE Guidelines and GIRFT
audits.standard: NICE guidelines and GIRFT recommendations for acute ureteric stones
audits.setting: East Surrey Hospital, Surrey and Sussex Healthcare NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Serum calcium checked 47%; dietary advice 17%; stents without clear indication or sepsis 83%; conservative management 65%; urgent treatment within 48 hours 35%.

audits.intervention: Hot primary URS theatre opened and efforts to improve follow-up.

cycle2.result: Serum calcium 66%; dietary advice 72%; stents without clear indication 57%; conservative management 46%; urgent treatment within 48 hours 53%.

audits.other_findings: Lost hot stone clinic follow-ups fell significantly. Staffing and lack of CEPOD support limited primary URS.
audits.citation: Hossain A, Papikinos P. 195 Close Loop Retrospective Audit of Acute Ureteric Stone Management: A Comparison with NICE Guidelines and GIRFT. British Journal of Surgery. 2025;112(Supplement_10). doi:10.1093/bjs/znaf128.216.

audits.title: Improving the effectiveness of the emergency management of renal colic in a district general hospital: a completed audit cycle.
audits.standard: New local guidelines based on literature (diclofenac analgesia, prompt IVU)
audits.setting: Emergency department, district general hospital (East Surrey Hospital, Redhill)

cycle1.result: 7 of 14 admitted, 5 to wait for IVU; mean IVU wait 12.3 (SD 2.2) hours; mainly intramuscular opioids.

audits.intervention: New interdepartmental guidelines, junior doctor training, ED staff performing 3-film IVUs

cycle2.result: 5 of 19 admitted, 1 waiting for IVU; mean IVU wait 4.1 (SD 0.96) hours; rectal diclofenac the drug of choice.

audits.citation: Kastner C, Tagg A. Improving the effectiveness of the emergency management of renal colic in a district general hospital: a completed audit cycle. Emerg Med J. 2003;20(5):449-450. doi:10.1136/emj.20.5.449. PMID: 12954686.

audits.title: The management of ureteric stones in the Accident and Emergency department.
audits.standard: Appropriate admission or discharge of patients with radiologically proven ureteric stones (no specific criteria existed at baseline)
audits.setting: Accident and Emergency department, Croydon University Hospital

cycle1.result: No easily accessible, specific criteria were used to guide which patients were admitted and which discharged.

audits.intervention: Admission criteria and a discharge proforma were developed and implemented in A&E.

cycle2.result: Fewer unnecessary admissions and fewer inappropriate discharges (no figures given in abstract).

audits.citation: Dawson K, Dawson L. The management of ureteric stones in the Accident and Emergency department. BMJ Qual Improv Rep. 2014;2(2):u615.w1458. doi:10.1136/bmjquality.u615.w1458. PMID: 26734220.

audits.title: Audit of the Acute Management of Renal Colic in District Hospitals Within a National Health Service Trust.
audits.standard: NICE and BAUS renal colic guidelines, including CT-KUB within 24 hours and NSAID analgesia
audits.setting: District hospitals within an NHS Trust in the West Midlands

cycle1.result: CT-KUB mean completion time nine hours; 7.7% beyond 24-hour benchmark; stone detection rate 41.2%.

audits.other_findings: NSAIDs were under-used; stone detection higher in males (54%) than females (27.5%).

audits.title: Improving the Acute Management of Ureteric Stones in a District General Hospital: A Two-Phase Quality Improvement Study Evaluating Practice Against NICE NG118 and GIRFT Recommendations.
audits.standard: NICE NG118 and GIRFT recommendations for acute ureteric stones
audits.setting: District general hospital (Surrey and Sussex Healthcare NHS Trust)

cycle1.result: CT KUB within 24 hours 98%; urgent intervention within 48 hours 35%; non-indicated stent placement 83%; lost stent follow-up 2 patients; hot clinic follow-up loss 16 patients.

audits.intervention: Primary ureteroscopy and day-case ESWL pathway, electronic stent recall protocol, Cerner auto-text discharge summaries, posters, presentations and clinician education.

cycle2.result: CT KUB within 24 hours 100%; urgent intervention within 48 hours 53% (p=0.028); non-indicated stents 57% (p=0.001); lost stent follow-up 0 (p=0.042); hot clinic follow-up loss 1 patient.

audits.other_findings: Authors suggest adding the MIMIC score to CT reporting.
audits.citation: Hossain A, Fozo K, Papikinos P. Improving the Acute Management of Ureteric Stones in a District General Hospital: A Two-Phase Quality Improvement Study Evaluating Practice Against NICE NG118 and GIRFT Recommendations. Cureus. 2025;17(8):e89902. doi:10.7759/cureus.89902. PMID: 40951126.

audits.title: Compliance with NICE, BAUS, RCR, and RCEM Guidelines for Acute Renal Colic: A Two-Cycle Quality Improvement Study at Lister Hospital Emergency Department, United Kingdom.
audits.standard: NICE NG118/QS195 (CT-KUB within 24 h, serum calcium), BAUS (CT-KUB within 14 h, calcium and urate, avoid repeat CT within 3 months), RCR iRefer and RCEM four-hour standard. Local targets: four-hour compliance ≥90%; CT-KUB request and report ≤90 min each; >90% scans within imaging windows; STONE score documentation ≥75%; calcium ≥65%, urate ≥20%; ≥30% reduction in repeat CT.
audits.setting: Emergency department, Lister Hospital, East and North Hertfordshire NHS Trust (district general hospital)

cycle1.result: Median urine dip turnaround 144 min, CT-KUB request 166 min, CT report 124 min; RCEM four-hour compliance 16.7% (19/114); calcium tested 50.9% (58/114); urate 0% (0/114); STONE score 5.3% (6/114); repeat CT within 3 months 19.3%; median ED stay 7.5 h.

audits.intervention: 'Straight to CT' pathway with registrar-requested scans, mandatory STONE score prompts in ICE/iRefer requests, three staff training sessions with prompt cards and intranet guides, dedicated porter slots and fast-track radiology queue with hot reporting, early SAU/CDU transfers.

cycle2.result: Urine dip 68 min, CT request 75 min, CT report 70 min (all p<0.001); four-hour compliance 57.0% (65/114; p<0.001); calcium 65.8% (75/114; p=0.022); urate 25.4% (29/114); STONE score 78.9% (90/114); repeat CT 9.6% (p=0.038); ED stay 3.9 h.

audits.other_findings: Diagnostic yield rose non-significantly from 57.9% to 68.4% (p=0.090) and alternative diagnoses fell from 11.4% to 7.0%; four-hour compliance remained below the 90% target.
audits.citation: Nehvi A, Ofedie A, Salahuddin SM, Akhtar F, Shrestha B, Faruqui S. Compliance with NICE, BAUS, RCR, and RCEM Guidelines for Acute Renal Colic: A Two-Cycle Quality Improvement Study at Lister Hospital Emergency Department, United Kingdom. Cureus. 2025;17(9):e93387. doi:10.7759/cureus.93387. PMID: 41024753.
